chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim, from Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Ata, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him):
Indeed, the people say: Indeed, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: The best place for Ihram is from the courtyard of your family.

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) rejected that and said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was from the people of Medina, and his designated place (miqat) was from Dhi al-Hulayfah, and there was only a distance of six miles between them. And if it were superior, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would not have entered Ihram from Medina. But Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: Enjoy your garments until your designated time.

key_terms.أَمْيَال: Plural of mile, a unit of distance
key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.دُوَيْرَة: Courtyard or enclosed area of a house
key_terms.وَقْت: Designated place or time for ritual entry

ai.seo_question: What is the best place to enter Ihram for Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration in *Mani al-Akhbar* to clarify the distinction between the Prophet’s established Sunnah and the specific practice of Imam Ali (peace be upon him). Imam al-Sadiq refutes the claim that Ali preferred the home courtyard by highlighting that the Prophet, despite living in Medina, traveled to Dhi al-Hulayfah, proving that the Prophet’s choice was based on divine designation rather than mere convenience or proximity. The hadith concludes by reconciling the two views: while the Prophet set the miqat at Dhi al-Hulayfah, Ali’s instruction to 'enjoy your clothes until your time' refers to the permissibility of wearing fine garments until the moment of entering Ihram, a point of scholarly nuance in fiqh.
